newsitem.title: UK: EMU decision not needed for a year - Labour's Cook.
newsitem.headline: EMU decision not needed for a year - Labour's Cook.

text.p: Britain need not decide whether to sign up for European Economic and Monetary Union or not for another year, the opposition Labour Party's foreign affairs spokesman Robin Cook said on Tuesday. "A decision will have to be made, probably towards the end of next year," Cook said on BBC radio. "We can see advantages in a single currency but to get those advantages we have to be confident...that British industry is able to compete on level terms within the single currency."
He said anything a Labour government decided on EMU will be "in the economic interests of the nation."
Cook was speaking at the start of the second day of the Labour Party's annual conference in Blackpool. Later today Labour leader Tony Blair will address the conference.
